top_story.headline: Federal prison in Mississippi plans to hire FlixBus, a commercial intercity bus line, without competition
top_story.dek: The Bureau of Prisons says FlixBus is the only company whose routes pass through Yazoo City.
paragraphs: The Federal Bureau of Prisons' Federal Correctional Complex Yazoo City in Mississippi intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract for fiscal 2027 commercial long-distance bus transportation to FlixBus North America. The notice of intent was posted on SAM.gov on November 3 as a Special Notice. It describes scheduled passenger bus routing to and from the prison to meet 'critical operational transportation needs, official passenger movement, and regional transport connectivity.' No dollar value is given.

The stated reason is that FlixBus is the only company with a 'proprietary intercity network and established commercial routes passing directly through the immediate geographic footprint of Yazoo City.' The notice says any other provider would need 'a custom, non-commercial route approach,' which it says would duplicate costs and cause delays.

A consumer intercity bus brand is an unusual counterparty for a federal prison, and USAspending shows no federal contract on record under the name FlixBus North America since fiscal 2008. The notice says it is not a request for competitive proposals, but other firms may send capability statements showing 'identical commercial intercity passenger route infrastructure' by November 18, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. The document gives that time as Eastern in one place and Central in another.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers asks to add $498 million to a repair contract so missile-defense power enclosure sites can be built by 2028
meta: $498 million added to a $450 million shared ceiling
only one company can do it
Department of the Army, Army Engineering and Support Center, Huntsville
blocks.text: The U.S. Army Engineering and Support Center, Huntsville wants the shared ceiling on its Facilities Repair and Renewal VI multiple-award contract raised from $450 million to $948 million, solely for the Missile Defense Agency's Modular Power Enclosures Program. The document says every task order must be awarded before the end of March 2027 and finished by February 2028, citing guidance from the Office of the Secretary of War received July 9, 2026. It limits the work to the 21 current holders because they already have 'existing subcontracting relationships, confirmed scope coverage, active ordering infrastructure.' No time is added to the contract.

blocks.title: Air Force rushes sole-source electrical rebuild at Shaw Air Force Base, citing the Middle East war and U.S. casualties
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Air Force, 20th Contracting Squadron
blocks.text: The justification authorizes Stanley Drake Construction to replace generators, transformers, switches and backup power in Building 1921 at Shaw Air Force Base, South Carolina. It says the building supports 'secure operations, intelligence processing, and command and control functions' for Operation EPIC FURY. It argues that war-driven tempo leaves no time to compete and warns of a power failure 'magnified by the current conflict in the Middle East, which has already resulted in significant American casualties.' The document is dated March 2026 and was posted November 3; the input does not give the award date.

blocks.title: Army medical research lab in Tbilisi to keep paying utilities through Georgia's national disease control center, without competition
meta: National Center of Disease Control and Public Health (Georgia)
only one company can do it
Defense Health Agency, for the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research
blocks.text: The Defense Health Agency says it intends to negotiate a sole-source deal with the National Center of Disease Control and Public Health in Tbilisi, Georgia for natural gas, electricity, water and waste services for the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research. The institute's Europe-Middle East office shares the Richard M. Lugar Center for Public Health Research with the center's staff. The agency's reason is that the two are co-located and the center is responsible for paying the utility provider. The counterparty is a foreign public health agency, not a commercial utility. The notice was posted as a Special Notice, says 'no solicitation document exists,' and asks for capability statements by 2:00 p.m. Eastern on November 17, 2026.

blocks.title: Air Force plans $280,000 sole-source contract with the Catholic Diocese of Wichita for a base chapel priest
meta: only one company can do it
Department of the Air Force, 22nd Contracting Squadron
blocks.text: The Catholic Diocese of Wichita would supply a Roman Catholic priest for the chapel community at McConnell Air Force Base: masses, reconciliation, funerals and office hours. The Air Force's determination calls the diocese 'the only known responsible source reasonably available.' The priest must be in good ecclesiastical standing, authorized to minister in the diocese, endorsed under Archdiocese for the Military Services requirements and eligible for base access. The document says market research ran from June 10 through October 22, 2026 and found other sources that did not meet the full requirement. It was posted as a Special Notice and is a single-source determination under simplified purchase rules.

blocks.title: NASA plans a $95 million, five-year sole-source follow-on with Draper for spacecraft guidance work, plus an $18 million increase on the current deal
meta: The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory, Inc.
$95 million not-to-exceed, plus an $18 million ceiling increase
only one company can do it
National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Johnson Space Center
blocks.text: One justification covers a single-award contract for The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory, Inc. with a five-year ordering period of June 1, 2026 through May 31, 2031 at a not-to-exceed $95 million. A second raises the ceiling of the current contract, 80JSC021DA005, by $18 million. The follow-on document says the predecessor contracts NNJ11HA31C, NNJ16HK08B and 80JSC021DA005 were all sole-source awards to Draper, and that moving to another contractor would take at least two years. The agency leans on Draper's Apollo-era guidance heritage for the Orion spacecraft and the Artemis moon program.

sections.headline: Defense Logistics Agency seeks a national supplier of epinephrine auto-injectors for the military, Veterans Affairs, prisons and tribal health

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency seeks a national supplier of epinephrine auto-injectors for the military, Veterans Affairs, prisons and tribal health
blocks.text: The Defense Logistics Agency wants a national requirements contract for 0.3 mg epinephrine auto-injectors, two to a bottle, as an unrestricted, fully competitive buy. According to the solicitation, customers served through pharmaceutical prime vendor programs include the Defense Logistics Agency, Department of Veterans Affairs, Bureau of Prisons and Indian Health Service, with annual usage 'estimated in the Schedule of Supplies.' It says offerors whose facilities are the subject of an FDA Warning Letter 'may not be considered to be technically acceptable.'

It intends a single indefinite-delivery contract and gives no dollar value.
